body:
[aida:product] #2027 merged. #2033 is the hard one and I am reporting a FAILED falsification on my own work before it goes anywhere near you.

TWO OF THREE DONE. #2026 merged 62a1396adf, #2027 merged 8bc2512480. Four merges from this seat tonight counting STORY-1419 and BUG-1546.

NOW #2033, AND THE HONEST STATE OF IT.

I wrote the executable latency test the reviewer asked for. Both tests passed. Then I restored `backend.load()` in the show path to falsify them, AND THEY STAYED GREEN. My test did not catch the regression it exists to catch.

I am telling you this before fixing it because the shape matters: the reviewer's finding was that the old guard "can pass while another expensive operation regresses the command". My replacement had THE SAME DEFECT in a more expensive form — it ran the command, timed it, and still passed with the regression restored. Shipping that would have satisfied the letter of the finding and left the property untested, and both of us would have called it done.

I DID NOT GUESS WHY. I instrumented the test and measured, with the regression in place:

    list=139ms   show=250ms   show_no_git=241ms   ratio=1.79   store_bytes=1,232,186

So the fixture WAS the 1.2 MB I intended — construction was fine. A full load over it costs ~110ms against ~139ms of process startup, and 1.79x is under any bound worth setting. The decoy was the right idea at the wrong dimension.

THE NUMBER THAT FIXES IT, measured on the real store rather than assumed: `aida show` takes ~10s over 4226 objects totalling 13.5 MB. That is ~2.4 ms PER OBJECT. Per-file overhead dominates per-byte cost by an order of magnitude, so the discriminating fixture is MANY SMALL OBJECTS, not one large one. 500 decoy objects should put a full load near 1.2s, which clears both the ratio bound and the spec's own 1-second ceiling.

The decoys are copies of an object the product itself wrote, with only id/spec_id/agreed_id rewritten, and the file is LOCATED BY SEARCH rather than by constructing objects/TYPE/000/. Hand-written YAML would encode my assumption about the schema instead of the product's actual output — the same mistake as the #2027 parser that targeted a `Relationships:` section `aida show` does not emit.

THE GREEN IS NOT EVIDENCE UNTIL I RE-RUN THE MUTATION AGAINST THE NEW FIXTURE. That is the whole reason this got rebuilt, and I will not report it as done on a pass alone.

ONE PIECE OF LIVE EVIDENCE FOR THE REVIEWER, measured on the current binary rather than quoted from the filing: `aida usage --json --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events` on this repo returns MY OWN show calls from minutes ago at 9.8 to 10.1 seconds each. I hit the bug four times while working on its fix. That is the population the spec's verification line points at, and it is still live on main.

No action needed from you. Reporting because a failed falsification on my own work is worth more to you than a green test result, and because if I had not run it you would have merged a guard with the defect it was written to remove.
subject: #2027 merged; #2033 falsification FAILED on my own test — it passed with the regression restored, cause measured not guessed
